memory_update.text: AXTI should be carried forward as the most direct US-listed underfollowed substrate candidate for the optical_interconnect_substrates node, but survival requires proof of datacenter optical InP revenue, customer qualification, and backlog/capacity tightness.

VECO should be tracked as an adjacent equipment-capacity signal for InP photonics rather than a direct substrate supplier; InP tool orders may be an early indicator of customer capacity expansion for AI optical interconnects.
COHR is a reference anchor, not an underfollowed discovery candidate; use it to validate 800G/1.6T demand, InP component requirements, and upstream supplier qualification bottlenecks.
ALMU belongs in the speculative_shadow lane only until filings or customer evidence show 800G/1.6T datacenter photonics qualification or production revenue.

The exact identity and public-market mapping of the 'fewer than six' qualified commercial-grade substrate suppliers remains unresolved; next pass should search primary sources for Sumitomo Electric, AXT, II-VI/Coherent supplier disclosures, and private/Asian suppliers to estimate concentration.

node: Precision optical substrates and materials for 800G/1.6T transceivers
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the optical-substrate chokepoint with a two-lane funnel: COHR as the high-attention reference validator for InP-based 800G/1.6T optics, and AXTI, VECO, and ALMU as underfollowed or speculative second-order mappings. The strongest direct underfollowed candidate is AXTI because it is explicitly an InP/GaAs/Ge substrate supplier tied to data-center connectivity. VECO is an adjacent equipment chokepoint for InP photonics manufacturing. ALMU is a speculative shadow candidate because its large-diameter compound-semiconductor-on-silicon platform could matter if native InP substrate availability becomes more constrained, but commercial proof for 800G/1.6T remains weak in the gathered evidence.
